item.title: Former Angelo State QB Fuller Signs with University of Arkansas
item.description: FAYETTEVILLE, AR — Former Angelo State quarterback Braeden Fuller has decided to play his final season for the University of Arkansas.Fuller entered the NCAA transfer portal after a rough 2025 season in which he injured his calf in Week 2 and ended up splitting reps after returning. Learn More Here.

item.title: Second Teen Dies in Frisco Sledding Crash
item.description: FRISCO, TX — A second 16-year-old girl has died following a sledding accident in Frisco last weekend.Gracie Brito reportedly died Tuesday night at a hospital after suffering life-threatening injuries in the crash. The other victim, Elizabeth Angle, also 16, died shortly after the accident Sunday. Both girls were sophomores at Wakeland High School. Learn More Here.

item.title: Former Lubbock Star Chavez on a Tear for No. 10 Oklahoma
item.description: NORMAN, OK — Aaliyah Chavez hasn’t taken long to become a force in the world of women’s college basketball.The former top-ranked recruit in the nation out of Lubbock Monterey High School was named the SEC Freshman of the Week on Tuesday for the sixth time this season.Chavez has stepped right into the starting lineup for No. 10-ranked Oklahoma and leads the Sooners with 19.1 points per game.She helped Oklahoma upset No. 2 South Carolina last Thursday, followed by a road win over Auburn on Sunday.

item.title: WATCH: Angelo State Rams Look to Stop the Skid
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — The Angelo State men’s basketball team will look to snap a three-game losing streak Thursday evening against UT Permian Basin, the last team the Rams defeated. Angelo State earned an 80-77 victory over the Falcons on Jan. 13 inside the Junell Center–Stephens Arena.The Rams dropped both games of a home-and-home series against Texas A&M-Kingsville last week, falling 67-64 last Wednesday in San Angelo before the Javelinas claimed a 58-56 win Saturday in Kingsville. Learn More Here.

item.title: NFL Hall of Fame Snubs Arguably the Greatest Coach of All Time
item.description: NEW YORK, NY — Bill Belichick, the eight-time Super Bowl–winning coach widely regarded as one of the greatest in NFL history, was not elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame in his first year of eligibility, according to multiple reports.ESPN reported that Belichick did not receive the required 40 of 50 votes from the Hall of Fame Selection Committee earlier this month. A Hall representative informed Belichick on Friday that he will not be inducted this summer in Canton, Ohio. Learn More Here.

item.title: WATCH: 4 Vehicle Crash on North Chadbourne Sends 1 to Hospital
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — A major crash on North Chadbourne has closed down lanes of traffic while crews work the scene.Around 2:45 p.m., a major crash was called at the intersection of 19th Street and North Chadbourne. Reporters on scene observed a minivan with major front-end damage and a Chevy truck with damage to the rear end. Learn More Here.

item.title: Ballinger Girls Survive Back-and-Forth Battle With Miles
item.description: BALLINGER, TX — When the Ballinger and Miles girls basketball teams get together, you can bet on seeing a close game.For the fourth straight time, the Runnels County rivals had a game that was decided by three points or less when they met Wednesday in Ballinger. Learn More Here.

item.title: Ballinger Boys Race Past Miles to Strengthen Playoff Chances
item.description: BALLINGER, TX — The Ballinger Bearcats had a chance to solidify their hold on the fourth and final playoff spot Wednesday against Miles.And they played like it from the opening tip.Ballinger sprinted out to a 19-2 lead by the end of the first quarter and cruised from there to a 66-42 win. Learn More Here.

item.title: Central Bobcats, Lady Cats Take Down Permian at Home
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — The Central Bobcats overcame a slow start to take down the first-place Permian Panthers in San Angelo on Wednesday night. Ean McNeill dropped 19 points for the Bobcats as Central claimed victory, 74-67.With the win, the Bobcats move into a 3-way-tie in first place in District 2-6A with Midland Legacy and Permian. Legacy defeated Odessa High on Wednesday night, 55-47. Learn More Here.
